name: Cataelano Mandaya
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Retired Glottolog entry, merged into Mandaya [mry] 2010; no Cataelano-specific description found

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Mandaya language', wikitext (cites Estrera 2020 for the phoneme tables)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Segmental tables only; lists 'Cateeleño' and 'Cataelano' among Ethnologue varieties; no stress.

sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2023. Ethnologue 26, entry 'Mandaya' [mry] (Internet Archive copy 2024-01-21)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; free view lists only vitality and 'Existing content: Dictionary'.

sources.citation: Duping, Arnold M. 2021. Phonological Variations among Mandaya Dialects: A Multiple Case Study. International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science 5(12): 380-386. doi:10.47772/ijriss.2021.51221
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Segmental inventory (23 phonemes) of the Cateel, Caraga, Manay and Tarragona dialects; Table 5 'Variations of Vowel Lengthening' notes lengthened /a:/ and /u:/ (Cateel has only /a:/ and /u:/ lengthened, p. 384) but stress/accent is never mentioned and no placement rule is given.

sources.citation: Galvez, Lilibeth. 2018. Isogloss of Mandaya lexemes: Looking into their linguistic variations. Davao Research Journal 12(1).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lexical isogloss study (Mati to Boston, incl. Cateel); mentions vowel lengthening in individual lexemes (e.g. hapon, unu:un) but gives no stress rule.

sources.citation: Pasion, Raymund M. & Mary Ann Sandoval. 2013. Varyasyong Ponolohikal ng Wikang Mandaya sa Ilang Munisipalidad ng Davao Oriental. Davao Research Journal 9(1): 58-66. doi:10.59120/drj.v9i1.30
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Segmental variation only (/h/, schwa, glide /l~l/) across Caraga, Manay, Baganga, Cateel. Recommendation 1 (pp. 65-66) explicitly calls for a future study of the suprasegmental phonemes 'tono, haba, diin at antala' (tone, length, stress, juncture), i.e. stress was not treated.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2009. Change Request 2009-068 (submitted by Bill Hall & Scott Burton, SIL Philippines): merge [mst] Cataelan Mandaya and [myt] Sangab Mandaya into [mry] Mandaya. 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Identity only: 'The present codes for Mandaya (mrt, mry, and mst) do not represent dialects of Mandaya but data collection points when Andrew Gallman was gathering data for his dissertation some 30 years ago. In reality it is all the same language' (p. 2).

sources.citation: Gallman, Andrew F. 1979. Proto-South-East Mindanao and its internal relationships. Papers in Philippine Linguistics No. 10 (Pacific Linguistics A-55), 1-52. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2 'The phonemic systems in PSEM' (pp. 6-9) gives only consonant and vowel correspondence sets for the eight SEM lects incl. MDK (Mandayan-Kabasagan = the Boston/Cateel point) and says 'There is no complete phonemic statement available for any of SEM languages except KLT and MSK' (p. 6); no statement on stress or vowel length for any Mandaya lect; the wordlist forms carry no accent marks. The only 'stress' hits in the text are in the Proto-Danaw section and in another paper (Chamorro) bound in the same PL volume.

sources.citation: Estrera, Edward G. 2020. A Grammatical Sketch of Mandaya. Diliman, University of the Philippines: Ms. 56 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only grammar sketch of Mandaya and Glottolog tags it as the Mandaya of Cateel, i.e. exactly the Cataelano variety; Wikipedia's phoneme tables come from it, so its phonology section almost certainly covers stress/length. Hammarström holds a PDF (hh: papua/); ask him or the author (UP Diliman Linguistics).
